consumer_seed: The Ofcom Connected Nations Spring 2026 update was published on 13 May 2026.
The report provides a snapshot of mobile coverage and fixed broadband availability as of January 2026.
Full fibre was available to 24.9 million UK residential premises, equal to 82% of 30.5 million homes.
Full-fibre availability increased by 1.2 million homes in the six months to January 2026.
Full-fibre take-up reached 12.4 million connections, equal to 47% of all premises with access to full fibre.
The Ofcom scam-call, text and message guide was published on 15 July 2026.
Ofcom advises people not to reply, click links, press buttons or share personal or financial details when a message may be a scam.
A suspected scam mobile-call number can be forwarded to 7726 free of charge so the mobile provider can investigate and potentially block it.
Ofcom states that it will never call a person out of the blue or ask for bank or personal details.
The Ofcom Map Your Mobile milestone article was published on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom reported that one million people had used the Map Your Mobile checker.
The checker lets users enter a postcode to see network availability and a performance score for their postal district.
Map Your Mobile combines crowdsourced Opensignal experience data with predictive information from UK mobile networks.
The Ofcom 2G and 3G switch-off guide was last updated on 29 May 2026.
Ofcom states that UK 3G mobile networks are now switched off.
All UK mobile network operators have confirmed that they will switch off 2G by 2033 at the latest, although individual operators may act earlier.
Customers already using newer 4G or 5G devices are unlikely to need hardware changes, though some devices may need software or settings updates.
expansion_rule: For each June/July comparable BDUK contract emit nineteen records: July supplier, July contracted, July built, June contracted, June built, contracted delta, built delta, built percentage change or zero-base guard, July ratio, June ratio, ratio percentage-point change, July contracted share, July built share, July contracted rank, July built rank, July ratio rank, built-delta rank, contribution to displayed total built increase, and transition classification. Append 17 Ofcom records. Competition ranks use descending competition ranking. Every fifth record is REVALIDATION; all others are UPGRADE.
